spec.description: Boston's subway live, twice: a line diagram laid out by Graphviz in the browser and the Kepler Plus fleet map, with every MBTA train on both. Click a station or a train on either.

options.content:
### Boston's subway, live — the line diagram and the map

Every MBTA subway train, twice: on a **line diagram that Graphviz lays out in your browser** from the MBTA's own patterns, and on the map. **Click a station** on either to fly the map there and list its next trains; **click a train** to follow it.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Red')::BIGINT AS "Red",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Orange')::BIGINT AS "Orange",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Blue')::BIGINT AS "Blue",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Green')::BIGINT AS "Green",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Mattapan')::BIGINT AS "Mattapan"
FROM $trains

spec.rawSql:
-- The network, one row per station of each canonical pattern. Names the
-- station variable so the diagram marks the station picked.
SELECT route, line, pattern, seq, station, name, latitude, longitude,
       station = $station AS picked
FROM $network

-- Where each train sits on the diagram: on the hop between two stations it is
-- running, and how far along it (0 to 1). The feed gives the station a train
-- is at or heading to; the hop is the one into that station on its route and
-- direction, and where two hops lead in (the Red Line at JFK/UMass, heading
-- north) the one starting nearer the train. How far along is the distance
-- from the station behind over the distance between both, in a straight line.
-- A train stopped at a station sits on it; one whose station starts its route
-- in that direction, too.
WITH e AS (
  SELECT route, station AS a, lead(station) OVER w AS b,
         latitude AS alat, longitude AS alng, lead(latitude) OVER w AS blat, lead(longitude) OVER w AS blng
  FROM $network
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY pattern ORDER BY seq)
),
-- Each hop both ways: a direction 1 train runs the pattern backwards.
hop AS (
  SELECT route, 0 AS dir, a AS f, b AS t, alat AS flat, alng AS flng, blat AS tlat, blng AS tlng FROM e WHERE b IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT route, 1 AS dir, b AS f, a AS t, blat, blng, alat, alng FROM e WHERE b IS NOT NULL
),
cand AS (
  SELECT tr.vehicle, h.f, h.t,
         -- Degrees of longitude are 0.74 of a degree of latitude in Boston.
         sqrt(((tr.longitude - h.flng) * 0.74) ^ 2 + (tr.latitude - h.flat) ^ 2) AS df,
         sqrt(((tr.longitude - h.tlng) * 0.74) ^ 2 + (tr.latitude - h.tlat) ^ 2) AS dt
  FROM $trains tr
  JOIN hop h ON h.route = tr.route AND h.dir = tr.dir AND h.t = tr.station
),
best AS (
  SELECT * FROM cand
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY vehicle ORDER BY df) = 1
),
-- Where the trip it is on now ends: the feed also lists the trips each train
-- will run next.
toward AS (
  SELECT trip, any_value(toward) AS toward FROM $arrivals GROUP BY trip
)
SELECT tr.vehicle, tr.unit, tr.line, tr.route, tr.dir, tr.status, tr.station,
       w.toward,
       coalesce(b.f, tr.station) AS from_station,
       coalesce(b.t, tr.station) AS to_station,
       CASE
         WHEN tr.current_status = 'STOPPED_AT' OR b.f IS NULL THEN 1.0
         ELSE greatest(0.05, least(0.95, b.df / nullif(b.df + b.dt, 0)))
       END AS progress,
       tr.latitude, tr.longitude,
       tr.vehicle = $train AS picked
FROM $trains tr
LEFT JOIN best b USING (vehicle)
LEFT JOIN toward w ON w.trip = tr.trip
WHERE tr.station IS NOT NULL

spec.description: The MBTA's canonical patterns (one per line and branch) as a graph: a node per station, an edge per hop between consecutive stations, laid out by Graphviz neato (Kamada-Kawai) from the stations' real positions with every hop asked to be the same length. Each dot is a train from the latest vehicle positions, on the hop into the station it is at or heading to, as far along it as its straight-line distance from the station behind says, and to the right of its direction of travel. Hover for the train or station; click a station to fly the map there and list its next trains, a train to follow it on the map.
spec.title: Line diagram — laid out by Graphviz in your browser

spec.rawSql:
-- Every subway train, for the fleet layer and its tooltip: where its trip
-- ends and the station it is at or heading to.
WITH toward AS (SELECT trip, any_value(toward) AS toward FROM $arrivals GROUP BY trip),
names AS (SELECT station, any_value(name) AS name FROM $network GROUP BY station)
SELECT t.vehicle, t.unit, replace(t.route, '-', ' ') AS route, t.line, t.type, w.toward,
       t.status || ' ' || coalesce(n.name, 'a stop off the network') AS now,
       t.heading, t.latitude, t.longitude, t.time
FROM $trains t
LEFT JOIN toward w ON w.trip = t.trip
LEFT JOIN names n ON n.station = t.station

-- The track of each pattern, in its line colour.
SELECT route, line, geojson FROM $tracks

-- Every station once, with the lines that call there.
SELECT station, any_value(name) AS name, string_agg(DISTINCT line, ', ' ORDER BY line) AS lines,
       any_value(latitude) AS latitude, any_value(longitude) AS longitude
FROM $network GROUP BY station

-- The station picked on the diagram or the map. Empty until then.
SELECT any_value(name) AS name, any_value(latitude) AS latitude, any_value(longitude) AS longitude
FROM $network WHERE station = $station GROUP BY station

spec.description: Each train from the latest vehicle positions is a fleet asset in its line colour, gliding to its new position on every refresh, with a trail of where it went, remembered by the map while the page stays open. Tracks are the shapes of the canonical patterns in the MBTA schedule data. Click a train to follow it (click the map elsewhere to stop), a station to list its next trains.
spec.title: The same trains on the map

spec.rawSql:
-- The next trains at the station picked, from the trip updates: line,
-- where each is going, and in how many minutes. Trips that end there are
-- left out, as on the platform screens.
WITH here AS (SELECT any_value(name) AS name FROM $network WHERE station = $station)
SELECT here.name AS station,
       CASE WHEN a.route LIKE 'Green-%' THEN replace(a.route, 'Green-', '') ELSE a.line END AS badge,
       CASE a.line WHEN 'Red' THEN '#E8473B' WHEN 'Orange' THEN '#F59A1B' WHEN 'Blue' THEN '#3C7DE0' WHEN 'Green' THEN '#1FA35F' ELSE '#E8473B' END AS colour,
       a.toward,
       CASE WHEN date_diff('second', now()::TIMESTAMP, a.time::TIMESTAMP) < 60 THEN 'now'
            ELSE round(date_diff('second', now()::TIMESTAMP, a.time::TIMESTAMP) / 60)::BIGINT || ' min' END AS due
FROM $arrivals a, here
WHERE a.station = $station AND a.toward IS DISTINCT FROM here.name
ORDER BY a.time
LIMIT 10

spec.description: From the trip updates feed: the next ten trains the MBTA predicts at the station picked on the diagram or the map, within 45 minutes, with where their trip ends. Trips that end at the station are left out.
spec.title: Next trains at the station picked

options.content:
**Sources.** The MBTA's GTFS Realtime feeds, *VehiclePositions* and *TripUpdates* ([cdn.mbta.com](https://www.mbta.com/developers/gtfs-realtime)), read on every refresh through the stack's gateway, whose 15 s cache keeps the MBTA at one request per refresh whoever is watching. The network and the tracks come from the MBTA's schedule data in [LAMP](https://performancedata.mbta.com)'s GTFS archive: the canonical route patterns, which the MBTA keeps for maps and diagrams, with their stops and shapes, in the version in force today in Boston. Nothing is stored: there is no history beyond the trail the map remembers while the page is open.

**The diagram.** Built in your browser on each visit: a graph with a node per station and an edge per hop between consecutive stations of a pattern, handed to [Graphviz](https://graphviz.org) compiled to WebAssembly ([Viz.js](https://github.com/mdaines/viz-js)). Its *neato* engine in Kamada-Kawai mode starts from the stations' real positions and moves them until every hop is as close as it can get to the same length. Where two lines share a hop it draws them side by side.

**Trains on the diagram.** The feed says which station a train is stopped at, arriving at or on its way to. It is drawn on the hop into that station on its route and direction (where two hops lead in, the one starting nearer the train), as far along as its straight-line distance from the station behind over the length of the hop. A train waiting at the first station of its trip sits on it. A few trains report no stop and are only on the map.

<small>Unofficial dashboard, not endorsed by or affiliated with the MBTA. Data: Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority, under the MBTA developer license.</small>

spec.title: Boston's subway live — Graphviz line diagram and map

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: the subway as the MBTA draws it. One row per
-- station of each canonical route pattern (the patterns the MBTA keeps for
-- maps and diagrams: both Red branches, the four Green branches), in the order
-- a direction 0 train serves them. The archive keeps every version of a row;
-- the one in force today in Boston wins. Seven days back picks the year, so
-- the first week of January still finds a file.
WITH today AS (SELECT strftime(now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York', '%Y%m%d')::INTEGER AS d),
patterns AS (
  SELECT route_id AS route, representative_trip_id AS pattern
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/route_patterns.parquet'), today
  WHERE (route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR route_id LIKE 'Green-%')
    AND canonical_route_pattern = 1 AND direction_id = 0
    AND gtfs_active_date <= d AND gtfs_end_date >= d
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY route_pattern_id ORDER BY gtfs_active_date DESC) = 1
),
calls AS (
  SELECT trip_id AS pattern, stop_id, stop_sequence
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/stop_times.parquet'), today
  WHERE trip_id LIKE 'canonical-%' AND gtfs_active_date <= d AND gtfs_end_date >= d
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY trip_id, stop_sequence ORDER BY gtfs_active_date DESC) = 1
),
stops AS (
  SELECT stop_id,
         arg_max(coalesce(parent_station, stop_id), gtfs_active_date) AS station,
         arg_max(stop_name, gtfs_active_date)                          AS name,
         arg_max(stop_lat, gtfs_active_date)                           AS latitude,
         arg_max(stop_lon, gtfs_active_date)                           AS longitude
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/stops.parquet')
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT p.route,
       CASE WHEN p.route LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Green' ELSE p.route END AS line,
       p.pattern,
       row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY p.pattern ORDER BY c.stop_sequence) AS seq,
       s.station,
       st.name,
       st.latitude,
       st.longitude
FROM patterns p
JOIN calls c USING (pattern)
JOIN stops s ON s.stop_id = c.stop_id
-- Named and placed as the station, not the platform the pattern stops at.
JOIN stops st ON st.stop_id = s.station
ORDER BY p.pattern, seq

-- Server side, once per visit: the track of each canonical pattern, from the
-- shapes of the MBTA schedule data, for the map. Versions as in the network.
WITH today AS (SELECT strftime(now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York', '%Y%m%d')::INTEGER AS d),
patterns AS (
  SELECT route_id AS route, trip_id AS pattern, shape_id
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/trips.parquet'), today
  WHERE trip_id LIKE 'canonical-%' AND direction_id = 0
    AND (route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR route_id LIKE 'Green-%')
    AND gtfs_active_date <= d AND gtfs_end_date >= d
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY trip_id ORDER BY gtfs_active_date DESC) = 1
),
points AS (
  SELECT shape_id, shape_pt_sequence AS seq, shape_pt_lat AS lat, shape_pt_lon AS lng
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/shapes.parquet'), today
  WHERE shape_id IN (SELECT shape_id FROM patterns) AND gtfs_active_date <= d AND gtfs_end_date >= d
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY shape_id, shape_pt_sequence ORDER BY gtfs_active_date DESC) = 1
)
SELECT p.route,
       p.pattern,
       CASE WHEN p.route LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Green' ELSE p.route END AS line,
       ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_MakeLine(list(ST_Point(s.lng, s.lat) ORDER BY s.seq)))::VARCHAR AS geojson
FROM patterns p JOIN points s USING (shape_id)
GROUP BY ALL

-- Server side: every subway train in the latest vehicle positions. The feed
-- sends no CORS headers, so DuckDB in the grafana container reads it through
-- the gateway, whose 15 s cache keeps the MBTA at one request per refresh
-- whoever is watching. `station` is the station of the stop the train is at
-- or heading to (the feed names a platform). `vehicle` is the fleet asset and
-- `time` its ping; not `vehicle_id`, which the map would read as a trip.
-- One request per feed: http_get fetches the whole file at once, and the JSON
-- is parsed from memory; read_json would read it in several passes, and a pass
-- landing after the cache renews the feed fails DuckDB's ETag check.
WITH feed AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT (http_get('http://feeds/mbta/realtime/VehiclePositions_enhanced.json')->>'body')::JSON AS doc),
vp AS (SELECT (doc->>'$.header.timestamp')::BIGINT AS hts, unnest(json_extract(doc, '$.entity[*]')) AS e FROM feed),
v AS (
  SELECT hts,
         e->>'$.vehicle.vehicle.id'                       AS vehicle,
         e->>'$.vehicle.vehicle.label'                    AS unit,
         e->>'$.vehicle.trip.trip_id'                     AS trip,
         e->>'$.vehicle.trip.route_id'                    AS route,
         (e->>'$.vehicle.trip.direction_id')::INTEGER     AS dir,
         e->>'$.vehicle.stop_id'                          AS stop_id,
         e->>'$.vehicle.current_status'                   AS current_status,
         (e->>'$.vehicle.position.bearing')::DOUBLE       AS heading,
         (e->>'$.vehicle.position.latitude')::DOUBLE      AS latitude,
         (e->>'$.vehicle.position.longitude')::DOUBLE     AS longitude,
         (e->>'$.vehicle.timestamp')::BIGINT              AS ts
  FROM vp
),
sub AS (
  SELECT * FROM v WHERE route IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR route LIKE 'Green-%'
),
stops AS (
  SELECT stop_id, arg_max(coalesce(parent_station, stop_id), gtfs_active_date) AS station
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/stops.parquet')
  WHERE stop_id IN (SELECT stop_id FROM sub)
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT vehicle,
       unit,
       trip,
       route,
       CASE WHEN route LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Green' ELSE route END AS line,
       -- Picks the 3D model: a subway train for every line, the Mattapan trolley too.
       'subway'                                                    AS type,
       dir,
       s.station,
       current_status,
       CASE current_status
         WHEN 'STOPPED_AT'    THEN 'Stopped at'
         WHEN 'INCOMING_AT'   THEN 'Arriving at'
         WHEN 'IN_TRANSIT_TO' THEN 'On the way to'
         ELSE 'No status'
       END                                                         AS status,
       heading,
       latitude,
       longitude,
       to_timestamp(ts)                                            AS time,
       to_timestamp(hts)                                           AS feed_time
FROM sub LEFT JOIN stops s USING (stop_id)
WHERE latitude IS NOT NULL

-- Server side: when each subway train is expected at each station ahead of it,
-- from the trip updates feed, read like the positions. Only the next 45
-- minutes. `toward` is the last station the trip still has ahead, so a
-- short-turned train says where it really ends.
WITH feed AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT (http_get('http://feeds/mbta/realtime/TripUpdates_enhanced.json')->>'body')::JSON AS doc),
tu AS (SELECT unnest(json_extract(doc, '$.entity[*]')) AS e FROM feed),
trips AS (
  SELECT e->>'$.trip_update.trip.trip_id'                AS trip,
         e->>'$.trip_update.trip.route_id'               AS route,
         (e->>'$.trip_update.trip.direction_id')::INTEGER AS dir,
         e->>'$.trip_update.vehicle.id'                  AS vehicle,
         e
  FROM tu
  WHERE (e->>'$.trip_update.trip.route_id') IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan')
     OR (e->>'$.trip_update.trip.route_id') LIKE 'Green-%'
),
calls AS (
  SELECT trip, route, dir, vehicle, unnest(json_extract(e, '$.trip_update.stop_time_update[*]')) AS s
  FROM trips
),
c AS (
  SELECT trip, route, dir, vehicle,
         (s->>'$.stop_sequence')::INTEGER AS seq,
         s->>'$.stop_id'                  AS stop_id,
         coalesce((s->>'$.arrival.time')::BIGINT, (s->>'$.departure.time')::BIGINT) AS t,
         coalesce(s->>'$.schedule_relationship', 'SCHEDULED') = 'SKIPPED' AS skipped
  FROM calls
),
stops AS (
  SELECT stop_id,
         arg_max(coalesce(parent_station, stop_id), gtfs_active_date) AS station
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/stops.parquet')
  WHERE stop_id IN (SELECT stop_id FROM c)
  GROUP BY 1
),
names AS (
  SELECT stop_id AS station, arg_max(stop_name, gtfs_active_date) AS name
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/stops.parquet')
  WHERE stop_id LIKE 'place-%'
  GROUP BY 1
),
ahead AS (
  SELECT c.*, s.station, arg_max(n.name, c.seq) OVER (PARTITION BY c.trip) AS toward
  FROM c JOIN stops s USING (stop_id) LEFT JOIN names n ON n.station = s.station
  WHERE NOT c.skipped
)
SELECT trip,
       route,
       CASE WHEN route LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Green' ELSE route END AS line,
       dir,
       vehicle,
       station,
       toward,
       to_timestamp(t) AS time
FROM ahead
WHERE t BETWEEN epoch(now()) - 60 AND epoch(now()) + 45 * 60
